issues.label: Subject-matter jurisdiction basis
issues.why: Court must confirm jurisdiction properly arose under MCL 712A.2(b)(1) and (2).

issues.label: Plea validity and advisements
issues.why: No-contest plea must be knowing, voluntary, and supported by a factual basis with proper advisements.

issues.label: Effect of ICWA removal
issues.why: Court must ensure ICWA compliance for the removed child and that findings/orders for remaining children were not tainted by ICWA-related requirements or errors.

issues.label: Preliminary removal standards
issues.why: Court must confirm the “contrary to welfare” and reasonable-efforts-to-prevent-removal findings were properly made at removal.

issues.label: Placement legality and appropriateness
issues.why: Court must assess legality of the youngest child’s foster placement and the oldest child’s placement with her biological father/caregiver.

issues.label: Reasonable reunification efforts
issues.why: DHHS must make reasonable efforts to reunify (or show statutory exception), and the court must make/find them throughout the case.

issues.label: Adequacy of service plan (PATP)
issues.why: Services must be tailored to the barriers (medical neglect, SUD, mental health, parenting, housing, income) and updated appropriately.

issues.label: Timeliness of referrals/services
issues.why: Delays in psychological evaluation or treatment referrals can undermine reasonable efforts and due process.

issues.label: Access barriers to services
issues.why: Court must consider transportation, scheduling, cost/insurance, and availability of inpatient/SUD services affecting compliance.

issues.label: Communication and caseworker diligence
issues.why: Court must consider whether DHHS accurately monitored progress, verified claims, and promptly addressed noncompliance.

issues.label: Drug-screen reliability and process
issues.why: Court must consider validity, frequency, notice, chain-of-custody, and interpretation of positive methamphetamine screens.

issues.label: Need for inpatient treatment
issues.why: Given the psychological evaluation recommendation, court must consider whether DHHS reasonably pursued inpatient options and whether outpatient was sufficient.

issues.label: Mental health treatment efforts
issues.why: Court must consider whether mental-health interventions were offered/implemented consistent with evaluation recommendations.

issues.label: Parenting-time provision and support
issues.why: Court must determine whether parenting time was offered consistent with the case plan and whether barriers were addressed.

issues.label: Benefit from parenting education
issues.why: Completion of classes is insufficient; court must evaluate actual benefit/behavioral change and evidentiary support for lack of benefit.

issues.label: Housing stability findings
issues.why: Court must resolve disputes about housing stability, including lease enforceability and safety/appropriateness for children.

issues.label: Income/employment findings
issues.why: Court must determine whether respondent had/maintained legal, verifiable income sufficient to care for children and whether DHHS assisted reasonably.

issues.label: Medical neglect remediation
issues.why: Court must assess whether respondent remedied issues leading to the youngest child’s failure-to-thrive/medical neglect and can meet ongoing medical needs.

issues.label: Statutory ground identification
issues.why: Court must ensure the correct statutory subsection was applied (MCL 712A.19b(3)(c)(i) vs (c)(ii)) and supported by findings.

issues.label: 182-day requirement
issues.why: Termination under (c)(i) requires at least 182 days since initial dispositional order and the court must confirm timing.

issues.label: Conditions continue to exist
issues.why: Court must find the adjudication conditions (medical neglect, SUD, instability) still exist at termination by clear and convincing evidence.

issues.label: No reasonable likelihood of rectification
issues.why: Court must analyze likelihood respondent will rectify conditions within a reasonable time considering children’s ages.

issues.label: Proper “reasonable time” analysis
issues.why: Court must consider child-centered timelines, not indefinite opportunities, and weigh progress against duration of case.

issues.label: Use of other grounds not cited
issues.why: Court must avoid relying on unstated statutory grounds without notice and must ensure findings align with the cited ground.

issues.label: Evidentiary sufficiency standard
issues.why: Statutory grounds require clear and convincing evidence; court must ensure record meets that burden.

issues.label: Credibility and factual disputes
issues.why: Court must resolve conflicting testimony (e.g., housing, treatment participation) with explicit or supportable credibility determinations.

issues.label: Procedural due process at termination
issues.why: Respondent must have notice, opportunity to be heard, to present evidence, and to challenge DHHS evidence.

issues.label: Right to counsel and effectiveness
issues.why: Court must ensure respondent was represented and that any claims of ineffective assistance are addressed if raised/implicit.

issues.label: Best-interests determination
issues.why: After a ground is proven, court must decide by preponderance whether termination is in each child’s best interests.

issues.label: Individualized best interests per child
issues.why: Court must analyze best interests separately for the oldest and youngest children given different placements and needs.

issues.label: Bond and parenting ability
issues.why: Court must weigh the parent-child bond and respondent’s demonstrated parenting capacity against risks and instability.

issues.label: Child permanency and stability
issues.why: Court must consider children’s need for permanence, stability, and finality versus continued reunification attempts.

issues.label: Relative/parent placement factor
issues.why: Oldest child’s placement with her biological father (a parent/placement caregiver) affects best-interests analysis and may weigh against termination.

issues.label: Alternative dispositions short of TPR
issues.why: Court must consider whether guardianship, custody with father, or continued placement could protect children without terminating rights.

issues.label: Impact of termination on sibling ties
issues.why: Court should consider how termination affects sibling relationships, especially with one child removed under ICWA.

issues.label: Safety and risk of harm
issues.why: Court must assess current and prospective risk from continued meth use, mental health issues, and inability to meet medical needs.

issues.label: Compliance vs benefit distinction
issues.why: Court must distinguish mere participation from meaningful benefit and determine whether lack of benefit is adequately supported.

issues.label: Reasonable efforts vs futility
issues.why: Court must decide whether services were reasonable and whether respondent’s nonparticipation made additional efforts futile.

issues.label: Findings on DHHS reasonable efforts
issues.why: Court must make record findings on reasonable efforts, and appellate review requires an adequate explanation.

issues.label: Consideration of ADA accommodations
issues.why: If mental health or substance-use disorder qualifies as disability, court must consider whether reasonable accommodations were offered in services.

issues.label: Case plan changes and notice
issues.why: Amendments adding SUD requirements must be properly communicated and incorporated into orders so respondent has fair notice.

issues.label: Role of father/parental fitness
issues.why: Court must consider that the father is caring for the oldest child and whether his fitness/custody affects necessity of terminating mother’s rights.

issues.label: Proper appellate preservation
issues.why: Court may need to address whether reasonable-efforts or other objections were preserved or subject to plain-error review.

issues.label: Adequacy of trial court findings
issues.why: Court must make sufficiently specific factual findings and conclusions to permit meaningful appellate review.
